Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 1–2:

Surat al-Hijr

Makkiyyah [[Makki by consensus; this is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 5 / 61.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.

* *

﴿Alif. Lam. Ra.﴾ It has been said: its meaning is: "I am Allah, the All-Seeing" [[See what has preceded: 1 / 58-59.]]. ﴿These are the verses of the Book﴾, i.e., these are the verses of the Book, ﴿and of a Qur'an that makes clear﴾, i.e., and verses of a Qur'an that is clear [[In "b": yubayyin (makes clear).]], making clear the lawful from the unlawful and the truth from the falsehood.

If it is asked: why did He mention "the Book" and then say "and a Qur'an that makes clear", when both are one and the same?

We say: it has been said that each one conveys another meaning, for "al-Kitab" is that which is written, and "al-Qur'an" is that in which some parts are gathered together with others.

It has also been said: by "the Book" is meant the Torah and the Gospel, and by "the Qur'an" this Book.

﴿Rubama﴾ Abu Ja'far, Nafi' and 'Asim read it with the ba' lightened, and the rest read it with it doubled. Both are dialects. Rubba is for paucity and kam is for multitude. Rubba enters upon a noun, and rubama upon a verb. One says: "Rubba man jaa'ani" (a man came to me) and "Rubama jaa'ani rajul" (a man has come to me sometimes). Here, ma is added so that what follows it is a verb.

﴿Those who disbelieved will wish﴾ they would wish, ﴿had they been Muslims﴾.

They differed concerning the state in which the disbeliever wishes for Islam.

al-Dahhak said: it is the state of seeing directly (al-mu'aynah) [[There is a point to consider here, since the disbeliever at that time has no certainty about the state of the Muslims. See: al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 8 / 279.]].

It has been said: it is the Day of Resurrection.

The well-known view is that it is when Allah brings the believers out of the Fire.

It is narrated from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "When the people of the Fire gather in the Fire, along with them are those among the people of the qiblah whom Allah wills, the disbelievers will say to those in the Fire from among the people of the qiblah: 'Were you not Muslims?' They will say: 'Yes.' They will say: 'Then what did your Islam avail you, when you are with us in the Fire?' They will say: 'We had sins, and we were seized for them.' So Allah, exalted is He, will become angry on their behalf [with the bounty of His mercy] [[Omitted from "b".]] and will command that everyone among the people of the qiblah who is in the Fire be brought out of it. Then, at that time, those who disbelieved will wish they had been Muslims." [[Related by Ibn Jarir al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 14 / 2 (Halabi edition), and Ibn Abi 'Asim in "al-Sunnah" 1 / 405-406, and al-Hakim in "al-Mustadrak": 2 / 442, and he said: sahih, though they did not record it. al-Haythami said in "al-Majma'" (7 / 45): "al-Tabarani related it, and in its chain is Khalid ibn Nafi' al-Ash'ari, of whom Abu Dawud said: abandoned (matruk). al-Dhahabi said: this is an excess in the criticism, for Ahmad ibn Hanbal and others narrated from him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy." It is also attributed in "Kanz al-'Ummal" (14 / 541) to Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and al-Bayhaqi in "al-Ba'th wa'l-Nushur". See also: Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 2 / 547. al-Albani authenticated it in "Zilal al-Jannah fi Takhrij al-Sunnah" 1 / 406.]].

If it is asked: how does He say "rubama", when it is for paucity, while this wishing is frequent among the disbelievers?

We say: "rubama" is sometimes mentioned for multitude; or He meant that their preoccupation with the punishment does not free them for regret, and that this idea occurs to their minds only occasionally.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 4–9:**

﴿Never did We destroy a town but it had a decreed term.﴾ That is, [it was destroyed from] among the people of a town, ﴿but it had a known decree﴾, that is, a fixed term that cannot be advanced, and the punishment does not come upon them until they reach it, nor is it delayed from them.

﴿No community can outstrip its term, nor can they delay it.﴾ The "min" (ﷺ) here is a *silah* (a redundant particle, a grammatical term meaning one that adds no meaning and is only there to complete the structure). The meaning is that death does not come early or late. It was also said that the intended term is the decreed punishment.

﴿And they say﴾, meaning the polytheists of Makkah, ﴿O you to whom the Reminder has been sent down﴾, that is, the Qur'an, and by this they meant Muhammad (ﷺ). ﴿Indeed you are surely mad.﴾ They spoke of the Reminder being sent down in a mocking manner.

﴿Why do you not﴾ (*law ma*, meaning "why not", "would that") ﴿bring us the angels﴾ as witnesses testifying to your truthfulness regarding what you say, ﴿if you are among the truthful﴾, that you are a prophet.

﴿We do not send down the angels﴾. The people of Kufa, other than Abu Bakr, read *al-malā'ikata* with two nunations (in the accusative case, *naṣb*). Abu Bakr read it with a *tā'* (ta), with a *ḍamma* on it, and with a *fatḥa* on the *zāy*, as *al-malā'ikatu* (in the nominative case, *raf'*). The rest read it with a *tā'*, with a *fatḥa* on it, and with a *fatḥa* on the *zāy*, as *al-malā'ikatu* (in the nominative case, *raf'*).

﴿except with truth﴾, that is, with punishment. Had the angels descended, meaning [if they came] in their true form, they would have hastened the punishment. ﴿Nor would they then have been given respite﴾, that is, they would not have been delayed. The disbelievers had been asking for the angels to be sent down visibly, so God answered them with this. Its meaning is: if they descended in their true form, the respite would have been removed from the disbelievers and they would have been punished immediately.

﴿Indeed, it is We who sent down the Reminder﴾, meaning the Qur'an, ﴿and indeed We are its guardians.﴾ That is, We protect the Qur'an from the devils, who might add to it, subtract from it, or alter it. God Most High said: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. "Falsehood" here is Iblis; he is not able to add to it what is not part of it, nor to subtract from it what is part of it.

It was also said that the pronoun in *lahu* ("its") refers back to Muhammad (ﷺ), meaning: indeed We are guardians of Muhammad from whoever intends him harm, as His Majesty said: ﴿And God will protect you from the people﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 67].

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 15, verse 24:**

﴿And We have certainly known those of you who go before, and We have certainly known those who remain behind.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas said: By "those who go before" he meant the dead, and by "those who remain behind" he meant the living.

Al-Sha'bi said: "Those who go before" refers to the first generations, and "those who remain behind" refers to the later generations.

Ikrimah said: "Those who go before" are those whom Allah has created, and "those who remain behind" are those whom Allah has not yet created.[^1]

Mujahid said: "Those who go before" are the earlier generations, and "those who remain behind" are the community of Muhammad (ﷺ).

Al-Hasan said: "Those who go before" are those who hasten to obedience and goodness, and "those who remain behind" are those who are slow to them.[^2]

It was also said: "Those who go before" are those who stand in the front rows during prayer, and "those who remain behind" are those who stand in the back rows. The reason is that women used to come out to congregational prayer and stand behind the men. Sometimes a man in whose heart there was doubt would fall back to the last row of the men, and a woman in whose heart there was doubt would move forward to the first row of the women, in order to be close to the men. So this verse was revealed.[^3]

The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The best of the rows of men is the first, and the worst is the last; and the best of the rows of women is the last, and the worst is the first."[^4]

Al-Awza'i said: It means those who pray at the beginning of the time, and those who delay until its end.

Muqatil said: It means, by "those who go before" and "those who remain behind," those in the battle line.

Ibn 'Uyaynah said: It means those who give the greeting (of peace) and those who do not give it.[^5]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verse 27:**

﴿And the jinn, We created him before from the fire of the scorching wind.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: he is the father of the jinn, just as Adam is the father of mankind.

Qatadah said: he is Iblis, who was created before Adam.

It is also said: al-Jann is the father of the jinn, and Iblis is the father of the devils (shayatin).

Among the jinn there are believers and disbelievers, and they live and die. As for the devils (shayatin), there are no believers among them, and they will die when Iblis dies.

Wahb mentioned: among the jinn there are those who have offspring, eat and drink [like the children of Adam] [[Omitted from manuscript "A".]], and among the jinn there are those who are like the wind: they do not eat, do not drink, and do not procreate.

﴿from the fire of the samum﴾. The samum is a scorching wind that enters the pores of a person and kills him. It is also said: the samum is by day and the harur is by night.

It is narrated from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih: the samum is a fire without smoke, and thunderbolts (sawa'iq) come from it. It is a fire between the sky and the veil. When God decrees a matter, it tears through the veil and descends to what it was commanded. The rumbling (hadhdhah) you hear is the tearing of that veil.

It is also said: the fire of the samum is the flame of fire.

It is also said: "from the fire of the samum" means: from the fire of Hell.

It is narrated from al-Dahhak, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: Iblis was of a tribe of angels called the jinn, who were created from the fire of the samum, while the jinn mentioned in the Qur'an were created from a smokeless fire (marij min nar). **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 28–30:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And when your Lord said to the angels, "Indeed, I will create a human being from clay, from black mud altered in smell"﴾. That is: "I am going to create a human being." ﴿from clay, from black mud altered in smell﴾.

﴿So when I have proportioned him﴾: I made his form balanced and perfected his creation. ﴿and breathed into him of My spirit﴾: so he became a living human being. The rooh (spirit) is a subtle body by which a person lives, and He attributed it to Himself as an honour. ﴿then fall down before him in prostration﴾: a prostration of greeting, not a prostration of worship.

﴿So the angels prostrated, all of them together﴾ — those who were commanded to prostrate.

If it is said: Why did He say ﴿all of them together﴾ when the purpose was already achieved by His saying "So the angels prostrated"?

We say: al-Khalil and Sibawayh held that He mentioned it as emphasis (ta'kid).

Al-Mubarrad mentioned that it was possible that some of them prostrated, so He said "all of them" to remove this doubt; then it was possible that they prostrated at different times, so this doubt was removed by His saying "together" (ajma'un) [[This answer is clearer in "Masa'il al-Razi wa-ajwibatuha min gharib ayat al-tanzil," pp. 167–168. He said: "Sibawayh and al-Khalil said: it is emphasis after emphasis, which adds further firmness to the meaning and establishes it in the mind, so it is not a case of obtaining what is already obtained; rather the relation of 'ajma'un' to the whole sentence is like the relation of 'kullahum' to it. Al-Mubarrad said: His saying 'ajma'un' indicates that they gathered at the time of prostration, and 'kullahum' indicates that the prostration came from all of them; so it is as if He said: the angels all prostrated together at one time. Ibn al-Anbari chose this view. Al-Zajjaj and most of the scholars chose the view of Sibawayh, and they said: if the matter were as al-Mubarrad claimed, 'ajma'un' would be a circumstantial clause (hal), since the definition of a hal would apply to it; but it is not a hal, because it is in the nominative case, and because it is definite like the other words of emphasis."]].

Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated through Ikrimah: Allah, mighty and majestic, said to a group of the angels, "Prostrate to Adam," but they did not do so, so Allah sent a fire upon them and it burned them. Then He said to another group, "Prostrate to Adam," and they prostrated [[Recorded by al-Tabari in his Tafsir: 14/31. Ibn Kathir said (2/551): "There is room for doubt about the authenticity of this report from him; apparently it is from Isra'iliyyat, and he described it as a strange and wondrous report."]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 31–40:

﴿He said: I will not prostrate to a human whom You created from clay, from black mud molded.﴾ He meant: I am [[in "B" khayr.]] better than him, because he is from clay and I am from fire, and fire consumes clay.

﴿He said: Then get out of it﴾, that is, out of Paradise, ﴿for indeed, you are accursed﴾, expelled.

﴿And indeed, upon you is the curse until the Day of Recompense.﴾ It was said: the people of the heavens curse Iblis as the people of the earth curse him, so he is cursed in the heavens and on the earth.

﴿He said: My Lord, then reprieve me until the day they are raised.﴾ The wicked one intended that he would not die.

﴿He said: Indeed, you are of those reprieved until the day of the appointed time.﴾ That is, the time at which the creatures die, and it is the first blast (al-nafkha al-ula).

It is said that the period of Iblis's death is forty years, which is the interval between the two blasts.

It is also said: God's granting his request for respite was not an honour for him, but rather an increase in his trial and his wretchedness.

﴿He said: My Lord, because You have misled me﴾, that is, You caused me to go astray. It was said: You deprived me of Your mercy. ﴿I will surely make [evil] attractive to them on earth﴾, the love of this world and Your disobedience, ﴿and I will mislead them all﴾, that is, I will surely lead them astray.

﴿Except Your sincere servants among them.﴾ These are the believers who made their obedience and their affirmation of God's oneness (tawhid) sincerely for You. As for the one who reads the lam with a fatha (al-mukhlasin), it means: those whom You have purified by Your oneness and chosen.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 45–49:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs.﴾ That is, among orchards and rivers.

﴿Enter them﴾ That is, it will be said to them: enter Paradise ﴿in peace﴾, that is, in safety, ﴿secure﴾ from death, expulsion, and calamities.

﴿And We will remove﴾, that is, We will bring out ﴿whatever resentment is in their breasts﴾, which is enmity, hostility, rancor, and envy, ﴿as brothers﴾, which is in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl), ﴿on couches﴾, the plural of sarīr (couch), ﴿facing one another﴾, each one facing the other, none of them looking at the back of his companion's neck.

It is related in some reports: when the believer in Paradise wishes to meet his believing brother, the couch of each of them moves toward the other, and they meet and converse.

﴿No fatigue will touch them therein﴾, that is, no toil will afflict them, ﴿and they will not be removed from it﴾. This is the most explicit verse in the Qur'an concerning eternal abiding (khulūd).

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Inform My servants that I am the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: meaning, for those among them who repent.

It is narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) went out one day to a group of his companions while they were laughing. He said: "Do you laugh while the Fire is before you?" Then Jibril (peace be upon him) descended with this verse and said: "Your Lord says to you, O Muhammad: Why do you make My servants despair of My mercy?" **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 61–66:**

Lot said to them, ﴿You are a people unknown to me﴾, meaning: I do not know you.

They said, ﴿Rather, we have brought you that about which they used to doubt﴾, meaning: they doubted that it would descend upon them, and it is the punishment. He used to warn them of the punishment, but they did not believe him.

﴿And We have come to you with the truth﴾, with certainty. It was also said: with the punishment. ﴿And indeed, We are truthful﴾.

﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night and follow behind them﴾, meaning: go behind them. ﴿And let none of you look back﴾, so that they will not be alarmed by the punishment when it descends upon their people.

It was also said: God made this a sign for those among the family of Lot who would be saved.

﴿And proceed where you are commanded﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means Syria (al-Sham). Muqatil said: it means Zughar (in "B" it is "Za'ar", with an unpointed 'ayn, a sukun, and an open first letter, a place in the Hijaz). Yaqut al-Hamawi said in Mu'jam al-Buldan (3/142–143): "Zughar", with a ghayn, on the pattern of Zufar, is a village on the outskirts of Syria, and it is what Abu Dawud al-Iyadi meant when he said:
*"Like the writing of Zughar, its gold-plated tiles, from refined gold."*

It was also said: "Zughar" is the name of the daughter of Lot, peace be upon him, who settled in this village, so it was named after her. Hatim al-Ta'i said:
*"May the Lord of mankind water it with heavy and light rain, from the southern slopes of al-Sarah, from Ma'ab to Zu'ar."*

The mention of "Zughar" also occurs in the hadith of al-Jassasah, which Muslim recorded in al-Fitan under no. (2942), 4/2261–2264.

It was also said: al-Urdunn (Jordan).

﴿And We decreed to him that matter﴾, meaning: We concluded for the family of Lot that matter, that is, We confirmed the command that we were given concerning the people of Lot, and We informed him: ﴿that the last of these people will be cut off﴾. The recitation of Abdullah (Ibn Mas'ud) supports this, namely: "And We said to him, indeed the last of these people..." (qira'ah, a variant recitation). This means their root, ﴿cut off﴾, uprooted, ﴿entering at dawn﴾, when they enter the morning.

Lot said to them, ﴿You are a people unknown to me﴾, meaning: I do not know you.

They said, ﴿Rather, we have brought you that about which they used to doubt﴾, meaning: they doubted that it would descend upon them, and it is the punishment. He used to warn them of the punishment, but they did not believe him.

﴿And We have come to you with the truth﴾, with certainty. It was also said: with the punishment. ﴿And indeed, We are truthful﴾.

﴿So travel with your family in a part of the night and follow behind them﴾, meaning: go behind them. ﴿And let none of you look back﴾, so that they will not be alarmed by the punishment when it descends upon their people.

It was also said: God made this a sign for those among the family of Lot who would be saved.

﴿And proceed where you are commanded﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: it means Syria (al-Sham). Muqatil said: it means Zughar (in "B" it is "Za'ar", with an unpointed 'ayn, a sukun, and an open first letter, a place in the Hijaz). Yaqut al-Hamawi said in Mu'jam al-Buldan (3/142–143): "Zughar", with a ghayn, on the pattern of Zufar, is a village on the outskirts of Syria, and it is what Abu Dawud al-Iyadi meant when he said:
*"Like the writing of Zughar, its gold-plated tiles, from refined gold."*

It was also said: "Zughar" is the name of the daughter of Lot, peace be upon him, who settled in this village, so it was named after her. Hatim al-Ta'i said:
*"May the Lord of mankind water it with heavy and light rain, from the southern slopes of al-Sarah, from Ma'ab to Zu'ar."*

The mention of "Zughar" also occurs in the hadith of al-Jassasah, which Muslim recorded in al-Fitan under no. (2942), 4/2261–2264.

It was also said: al-Urdunn (Jordan).

**Ma'alim al-Tanzil (Commentary of al-Baghawi) on Surah 15, verses 79–84:**

﴿So We took vengeance upon them﴾ with the punishment. This happened because [[In "A" it is narrated.]] God sent the heat upon them for seven days. Then God sent a cloud, and they took refuge in it, seeking coolness. God then sent fire from it upon them, and it burned them. This is His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So the punishment of the Day of the Canopy seized them﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 189].

﴿And indeed they both﴾ meaning the two cities of the people of Lot and the companions of the Thicket ﴿are on a clear highway﴾, on a path that is evident and plain.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers﴾. Al-Hijr is the city of Thamud, the people of Salih, and it lies between Medina and Syria. ﴿The messengers﴾: He meant Salih alone. [[The plural is used because whoever denies one prophet, or disbelieves in him, has disbelieved in all the prophets, since belief is obligatory in every prophet whom God has sent to the people of the earth. Whoever rejects his prophethood out of envy, partisanship or desire ... it becomes clear that his belief in those prophets whom he does believe in, and his affirmation of them, is not legitimate faith. For a broader detailed treatment of this, see the "Majallat al-Buhuth al-Islamiyya", issue (16), under the title "Inna al-Din 'inda Allah al-Islam" by Uthman Jum'a Dumayriyya.]].

﴿And We gave them Our signs﴾, meaning: the she-camel, her offspring, and the well. The signs in the she-camel were her emerging from the rock, her great size, the nearness of her birth, and the abundance of her milk. ﴿But they turned away from them﴾.

﴿And they used to carve out homes from the mountains, secure﴾ from ruin and from the mountain falling upon them.

﴿So the Blast seized them﴾, meaning the blast of punishment, ﴿at morning﴾, meaning they entered upon the time of morning.

﴿So what they used to earn did not avail them﴾, namely the polytheism and the evil deeds.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 15, verse 88:**

God's words: ﴿Do not strain your eyes﴾ O Muhammad ﴿toward what We have given enjoyment to some pairs of them﴾, kinds of them ﴿among them﴾, that is, among the disbelievers, desiring it. God Most High forbade His Messenger ﷺ from desiring this world and competing with its people for it [[ساقط من "ب".]] [*Absent from manuscript "b".*]

﴿And do not grieve over them﴾, that is, do not be distressed over what has escaped you of sharing with them in this world.

Abu al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Abu Ja'far Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn al-Anazi informed us, Isa ibn Nasr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak informed us, Jahm ibn Aws informed us, who said: I heard Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam, and Abdullah ibn Rustum passed by him in his procession, and he said to Ibn Abi Maryam: "I truly desire to sit with you and to hear your talk." When he had gone on, Ibn Maryam said: I heard Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not envy a wicked person for his blessings, for you do not know what he will meet after his death. Indeed, for him with Allah is a Killer that never dies." This reached Wahb ibn Munabbih, so Wahb sent to him Abu Dawud al-A'war, who said: "O Abu so-and-so, what is the Killer that never dies?" Ibn Abi Maryam said: "The Fire." [[أخرجه مسلم في الزهد والرقائق، برقم (٢٩٦٣) ٤ / ٢٢٧٥، والمصنف في شرح السنة: ١٤ / ٢٩٣.]] [*Narrated by Muslim in the Book of Asceticism and Softening of Hearts, no. 2963, 4/2275, and by the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/293.*]]

أي: كثير الاستغناء. وقال المغيرة بن حبناء: كلانا غني عن أخيه حياته ... ونحن إذا متنا أشدُّ تغانيا

قال: فعلى هذا يكون المعنى: من لم يستغن بالقرآن عن الإكثار من الدنيا، فليس منا، أي: على طريقتنا. وأيّد ابن كثير تفسير سفيان بن عيينة للحديث فقال: وهو تفسير صحيح، ولكن ليس هو المقصود من الحديث. انظر: ابن كثير: ٢ / ٥٥٨. وردَّ الشافعي رحمه الله تفسير ابن عيينة بأنه لو كان معناه على الاستغناء، لكان "يتغانى" وتحسين الصوت هو يتغنى. انظر شرح السنة للبغوي: ٤ / ٤٨٧، وراجع حكم التغني بالقرآن واختلاف العلماء فيه وفي معناه في: فتح الباري: ٩ / ٦٩-٧٢، تفسير القرطبي: ١ / ١١ وما بعدها، التبيان في آداب حملة القرآن للنووي ص (٨٧-٩٠) .]] [*al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an, chapter "Whoever does not chant the Qur'an" (9/68), related from Abu Hurayrah as a marfu' report: "Allah has not given permission for anything as He has given permission to a Prophet to chant the Qur'an." Sufyan said: "Its interpretation is 'to be independent through it.'" Ibn Hajar said in Fath al-Bari (9/69): one may draw support from what Abu Dawud and Ibn al-Darис narrated, which Abu Awanah authenticated, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ubayd Allah ibn Nuhayk, who said: "Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas met me while I was in the market and said: 'Merchants and earners! Abu Ubayd approved the interpretation of "yataghanna" as "yastaghni" and said it is permissible in the speech of the Arabs, and he recited al-A'sha: "I was a man for a time in Iraq... light of the camel-saddle, long in *taghanni*," meaning: abundant in self-sufficiency. He said: according to this, the meaning is: whoever does not make himself independent of the abundance of worldly goods through the Qur'an, is not of us, that is, not upon our way. ﴿who made the Qur'an into fragments﴾. They divided it and made it into parts (aʿdaʾ), so they believed in some of it and disbelieved in some of it. ﴿So by your Lord, We will surely question them all﴾ on the Day of Resurrection,

﴿about what they used to do﴾ in the world. Muhammad ibn Isma'il said: A number of the people of knowledge said: (It is about) His saying, "There is no god but Allah" [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/67.]].

Ibn Abbas said: He will not ask them, "Did you do (such and such)?" because He knows them better than they know themselves; rather He will say, "Why did you do such and such?" So His saying, ﴿no question will be asked about his sin﴾ [al-Rahman: 39], means a question of seeking information, and His saying, ﴿We will surely question them all﴾, means a question of rebuke and reproach.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verses 94–95:

His words, exalted is He: ﴿So proclaim openly what you are commanded﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Make it manifest." And it is related from him: "Carry it out" (amdihi).

Al-Dahhak said: "Make it known" (a'lim).

Al-Akhfash said: "Separate" (ifraq), meaning: separate, by means of the Qur'an, truth from falsehood.

Sibawayh said: "Judge by what you are commanded" (iqdi bima tu'mar). The origin of al-sad' (ṣad') is al-fasl (separation), and al-farq (distinction). The Prophet (ﷺ) was commanded in this verse to make the call (da'wah) manifest.

It is related from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubaydah, who said: "He had been concealing himself until this verse was revealed, and so he and his companions went out." [[See: Zad al-Masir: 4/420.]]

﴿And turn away from the polytheists﴾. It was abrogated by the verse of fighting. [[See above, the commentary (6) on the tafsir of surah al-Hijr, verse (3), p. (368).]]

﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾. God, exalted is He, says to His Prophet (ﷺ): Proclaim the command of God, and do not fear anyone other than God, the Mighty and Majestic. Indeed, God is sufficient for you against whoever opposes you, just as He sufficed you against the mockers. They were five men from the chiefs of Quraysh: al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah al-Makhzumi, who was their leader; al-'As ibn Wa'il al-Sahmi; al-Aswad ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib ibn al-Harith ibn Asad ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza ibn Zam'ah; and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) had invoked against him, saying: "O God, blind his sight and bereave him of his child." Al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth ibn Wahb ibn 'Abd Manaf ibn Zuhrah; and al-Harith ibn Qays ibn al-Tulatilah. Jibril came to Muhammad (ﷺ) while the mockers were circling the House. Jibril stood up, and the Prophet (ﷺ) stood beside him. Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah passed by him, and Jibril said: "O Muhammad, how do you find this one?" He said: "An evil servant of God." Jibril said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he gestured toward al-Walid's shin. Then he passed by a man of Khuza'ah, an arrow-maker who was fletching his arrows, wearing a Yemeni cloak and dragging his waistwrap. A splinter of an arrow caught on his waistwrap, but his arrogance prevented him from "bending his head" [[In "b": yuTamin.]] to remove it, and it began to strike his shin and scratched it. He fell ill from it and died.

Al-'As ibn Wa'il passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "An evil servant of God." Jibril pointed to the sole of his foot and said: "I have sufficed you against him." He went out on his riding beast with two of his sons, taking a stroll, and dismounted in one of those mountain paths. He stepped on a thorny plant (shabraqah), and a thorn entered the sole of his foot. He said: "I have been stung, I have been stung." They searched but found nothing, and his foot swelled until it became like the neck of a camel, and he died on the spot.

Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "A wicked servant." He pointed with his hand to his eyes and said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he went blind.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Jibril struck him with a green leaf, and his sight was lost and his eyes ached, so he began striking his head against the wall until he perished.

In the narration of al-Kalbi: Jibril came to him while he was sitting at the base of a tree with his servant. He began striking his head against the tree and hitting his face with thorns. He cried out to his servant for help, and his servant said: "I see no one doing anything to you except yourself," until he died, while saying: "The Lord of Muhammad has killed me."

Al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "An evil servant of God, though he is my maternal cousin." He said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he pointed to his belly. He became thirsty and drank (his belly swelled), and he died after a while.

In another narration of al-Kalbi: he went out from his family, and the poisonous wind (samum) struck him, and he turned black until he became Abyssinian. He came to his family, but they did not recognize him, and they shut the door against him until he died, while saying: "The Lord of Muhammad has killed me."

Al-Harith ibn Qays passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "A wicked servant." He pointed to his head and said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he coughed up pus and died.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He ate a salted fish, and thirst overcame him, and he continued drinking water until his belly burst and he died. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/69–72; Zad al-Masir: 4/421–423; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/100–102; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 359–361; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/469–470; Sirah Ibn Hisham: 1/408–409.]] That is the meaning of His words: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾, against you and against the Qur'an.

Jibril said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he gestured toward al-Walid's shin. Then he passed by a man of Khuza'ah, an arrow-maker who was fletching his arrows, wearing a Yemeni cloak and dragging his waistwrap. A splinter of an arrow caught on his waistwrap, but his arrogance prevented him from "bending his head" [[In "b": yuTamin.]] to remove it, and it began to strike his shin and scratched it. He fell ill from it and died.

Al-'As ibn Wa'il passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "An evil servant of God." Jibril pointed to the sole of his foot and said: "I have sufficed you against him." He went out on his riding beast with two of his sons, taking a stroll, and dismounted in one of those mountain paths. He stepped on a thorny plant (shabraqah), and a thorn entered the sole of his foot. He said: "I have been stung, I have been stung." They searched but found nothing, and his foot swelled until it became like the neck of a camel, and he died on the spot.

Al-Aswad ibn al-Muttalib passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one?" He said: "A wicked servant." He pointed with his hand to his eyes and said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he went blind.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Jibril struck him with a green leaf, and his sight was lost and his eyes ached, so he began striking his head against the wall until he perished.

In the narration of al-Kalbi: Jibril came to him while he was sitting at the base of a tree with his servant. He began striking his head against the tree and hitting his face with thorns. He cried out to his servant for help, and his servant said: "I see no one doing anything to you except yourself," until he died, while saying: "The Lord of Muhammad has killed me."

Al-Aswad ibn 'Abd Yaghuth passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "An evil servant of God, though he is my maternal cousin." He said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he pointed to his belly. He became thirsty and drank (his belly swelled), and he died after a while.

In another narration of al-Kalbi: he went out from his family, and the poisonous wind (samum) struck him, and he turned black until he became Abyssinian. He came to his family, but they did not recognize him, and they shut the door against him until he died, while saying: "The Lord of Muhammad has killed me."

Al-Harith ibn Qays passed by him, and Jibril said: "How do you find this one, O Muhammad?" He said: "A wicked servant." He pointed to his head and said: "I have sufficed you against him," and he coughed up pus and died.

Ibn 'Abbas said: He ate a salted fish, and thirst overcame him, and he continued drinking water until his belly burst and he died. [[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 14/69–72; Zad al-Masir: 4/421–423; al-Durr al-Manthur: 5/100–102; al-Muharrar al-Wajiz: 359–361; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/469–470; Sirah Ibn Hisham: 1/408–409.]] That is the meaning of His words: ﴿Indeed, We suffice you against the mockers﴾, against you and against the Qur'an.

﴿Those who set up with God another god; but they will come to know﴾

And it is said: [their mockery] [[omitted from manuscript "b".]] and their dividing (of the Qur'an): it is that when Allah, mighty and majestic, sent down in the Qur'an Surat al-Baqarah, and Surat al-Nahl, and Surat al-Naml, and Surat al-'Ankabut, they would gather and say mockingly: this is in [[in manuscript "b" "to". And in al-Bahr al-Muhit: some of them said: the gnat is mine; another said: the ant is mine; and another said: the spider is mine, mockingly.]] Surat al-Baqarah, and one would say this is in Surat al-Nahl, and one would say this is in Surat al-'Ankabut [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 5/468.]]. So Allah, exalted is He, sent down: ﴿And We certainly know that your breast is distressed by what they say﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 15, verse 97–99:

﴿So glorify your Lord with His praise﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: pray by the command of your Lord. ﴿And be among those who prostrate﴾, i.e., among those who pray, the humble ones.

Al-Dahhak said: "So glorify your Lord with His praise": say, "Glory be to Allah and praise be to Him." "And be among those who prostrate": those who pray.

It is narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), whenever a grave matter distressed him, would turn to prayer (salah). [Abu Dawud related it in Prayer, chapter: The time of the Prophet's (ﷺ) standing in prayer at night: 2/94, from Hudhayfah, with the wording: "The Prophet (ﷺ), whenever a matter distressed him, would pray." Al-Mundhiri said: some of them mentioned that it was narrated as mursal. It is also related by Imam Ahmad in al-Musnad: 5/388, and by al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il in the story of the Trench, at length; see al-Kafi al-Shaf p. (7). It is related by al-Khatib in Tarikh Baghdad: 6/274. The author related it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 4/155, and al-Albani weakened it in his commentary on al-Mishkat: 1/416; however, al-Albani later graded it as hasan in Sahih Sunan Abi Dawud, no. 1171.]

﴿And worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾, i.e., death, which is certain. This is the meaning of what is mentioned in Surah Maryam: "And He has enjoined upon me prayer and zakah as long as I remain alive."

Al-Mutahhar ibn 'Ali al-Farisi informed us; Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Salihi informed us; 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Ja'far Abu al-Shaykh al-Hafiz informed us; Umayyah ibn Muhammad al-Saffar al-Basri narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Azdi narrated to us; my father and al-Haytham ibn Kharijah both said: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Shurahbil ibn Muslim, from Abu Muslim al-Khawlani, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was not commanded to gather wealth and be among the merchants, but I was commanded: ﴿Glorify your Lord with His praise, and be among those who prostrate, and worship your Lord until there comes to you the certainty﴾." [Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah: 2/131 as mursal, and al-Sahmi related it as mawsul in Tarikh Jurjan p. (342) from Ibn Mas'ud. al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur (5/105) to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Hakim in "al-Tarikh," Ibn Mardawayh, al-Daylami in "al-Firdaws," and Ibn 'Adi in al-Kamil: 5/1897. The author related it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/237, and in its chain is Shurahbil ibn Muslim, whom Ibn Ma'in declared weak. See al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil: 4/340.]

It is narrated from 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: The Prophet (ﷺ) looked at Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr approaching, wearing a sheepskin tied about him with a cord, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Look at this one whom Allah has illuminated in his heart. I saw him between his two parents, who nourished him with the finest food and drink, and I saw upon him a garment bought for him, or purchased for him, for two hundred dirhams, but the love of Allah and His Messenger led him to what you see." [Abu Nu'aym related it in al-Hilyah: 1/108 with a hasan chain; see al-Mughni 'an Haml al-Asfar by al-Iraqi 4/287.] And Allah knows best.
